articles.title: UK government expected to approve Jackdaw gas field
articles.description: The long-awaited decision about the controversial North Sea field is expected on Wednesday morning.
articles.summary: The Jackdaw gas platform and drilling rig stand east of Aberdeen in the North Sea The UK government is expected to announce a long-awaited decision on whether to approve the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea.
key_points: It is widely believed in Westminster that Jackdaw will be approved but that a decision on the Rosebank oil field off Shetland will not yet be made.
The question of whether to approve the two sites has become hugely politically significant and has been delayed for several months.

Multiple Whitehall sources have told BBC News the government would make an announcement on Jackdaw on Wednesday morning with the Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh expected to address MPs in the afternoon.

articles.title: Jobless rate falls but small firms cut back hiring
articles.description: Small firms cite labour costs as a key factor in scaling back hiring, the Office for National Statistics says.
articles.summary: The UK's unemployment rate has dropped to its lowest for more than year, but job vacancies have continued to fall as smaller businesses cut back on recruitment, official figures indicate.
key_points: The jobless rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, the lowest since July last year.
However, vacancies fell by 21,000 in the three months to September to 691,000, with the ONS saying small firms were citing labour costs as a key factor in scaling back hiring.
The figures are the last official snapshot of the jobs market before the Budget, and analysts said they indicated the jobs market was showing signs of recovery despite the weakness in hiring.

key_points: Across the board, the levy body is expecting production of beef, lamb, pork and dairy to fall over the next year.

UK beef production, for example, is set to fall to 896,000 tonnes in 2027, marking a year-on-year decline of 0.8%, with increased carcass weights expected to only partially offset lower cattle throughputs.

key_points: This latest outbreak, which first emerged in Pennsylvania, has now been traced to shellfish harvested from the Little Wicomico River.
The outbreak has so far led to five confirmed cases and has resulted in the closure of all shellfish harvesting activity on the river until 7 November.
Specifically, this action also applies to bivalve molluscs, including clams and oysters, but not crab or finfish, also known as “true fish”.

articles.summary: When you watch a symphony orchestra, you can see the conductor, the musicians and the instruments, but what is really magical is the invisible architecture that keeps them together: coordination.
key_points: The conductor is FP&A itself: setting direction, owning the decision, and remaining accountable for the outcome.
The musicians are our analysts and finance teams: providing the judgement and business context that no system can ever replace.
The instruments are our AI agents and data systems: continuous, scalable, and built to run in parallel.

articles.title: Measuring the Invisible: How CFOs Must Evaluate FP&A Talent in an AI-First Function — Part 3 of 3
articles.summary: Why output metrics fail in agentic finance — and what to measure instead.
key_points: In Parts 1 and 2, I argued that agentic AI does not shrink the FP&A role so much as relocate it [1] [2].
The routine production of a variance pack or a driver-based forecast moves to the agent; what remains for the professional is judgment in the probabilistic zone that the agent cannot be trusted to…
Part 1 set out the capability that judgment requires — the FP&A Agent Manager and a four-layer stack: Data & Tooling Literacy, Probabilistic Model Behaviour, Probability Theory, Control Design.
